project.name: 41 Callowhill Street sprinkler pump and tank upgrade
project.summary: Corvina Property Holdings, sole owner of a 1988 6-storey Class 5 office building over a Class 7a basement car park in North Sydney, replaces its single electric sprinkler pump with electric duty, diesel standby and jockey pumps and a 150 kL fire water storage tank in an enlarged basement pump room, while every floor stays tenanted. There is no fit-out: one complying development certificate under the Fire Safety Code and one AS 4000 lump sum contract.

firms: Calder Fire and Hydraulic Engineers Pty Ltd
streets: 41 Callowhill Street, North Sydney NSW 2060 (invented street in a real suburb)

documents.content: The fire services engineer's options report after the investigation. Sections: ## Existing system (existing building; sprinkler protected throughout to AS 2118.1; one electric pump boosting the town main; the sprinkler system is supplied from Sydney Water's reticulated town water main through the existing fire service connection; the hydrant system is unaffected and remains town-main fed through the existing booster; the building has no performance solutions), ## Test results (flow and pressure test at the test line; the Sydney Water statement; the main alone cannot meet the sprinkler demand), ## Options (A: larger single pump, rejected; B: electric duty pumpset, diesel standby pumpset, jockey pump and a 150 kL modular fire water tank, recommended), ## Recommended option (the tank fits within the existing basement store; no car spaces or external areas are affected; tank panels are carried in through the basement car park entry; no crane is needed; no heavy vehicle access is needed; the existing fire service connection is retained; Sydney Water confirmed the main is adequate to refill the tank; the backflow device is upgraded; the electrical engineer confirmed the MSB has capacity and a spare supply-side connection; diesel fuel storage within a bunded day tank; pump room floor drains to the car park sump to protect the pump room from flooding; the diesel exhaust discharges through the existing basement plant exhaust shaft, clear of tenancies, air intakes and neighbours; the weekly test run is not audible in the tenancies), ## Compliance (the design complies with the deemed-to-satisfy provisions; no performance solution is proposed; no special fire hazards; no structural fire assessment and no facade, cladding or tested-system fire departure is required; no specialist fire systems are needed; no vulnerable occupants; the works do not build over or next to any sewer main or water main; no public road works; no roof or hard-surface change and no on-site detention), ## Approvals and delivery (one complying development certificate under the Fire Safety Code of the Codes SEPP; AS 4000-1997 General conditions of contract, with special conditions; the contract is one construction stage; there is no staged construction), ## Impairment plan (all floors remain tenanted and in use throughout the works; Stage 1 cut-over out of hours with a hire pump and fire watch; Stage 2 commissioning; flood the tank for its hydrostatic test), ## Scope (the scope is limited to the fire pump and tank upgrade; no tenancy works are included; level 3 remains leased to the existing tenant and is not affected; existing sprinkler heads on every floor are unchanged).
